one_liner: Senior Treasury manager running a team that advises foreign finance ministries on budgeting, public financial management, and financial accountability reforms.
fit_summary: This GS-15 role requires a year at GS-14 level in direct supervision, managing international technical assistance for developing-country governments and senior public financial management. Daniel's M.A. in Global Affairs covers development topics, but his work has been domestic emergency management and public health, with no PFM or supervision at that level, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens and nationals) and to CTAP/ICTAP-eligible federal employees, so no prior federal status is needed.

One year of specialized experience at the GS-14 equivalent must cover all three areas: (1) direct supervisory management of staff or teams, (2) identifying, developing, or managing international technical assistance projects, and (3) public sector financial management or government financial accountability.
A Secret security clearance is required, so you must pass a background investigation and the hiring office will check suitability.
A one-year supervisory probationary period may apply, and you would need to file a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report within 30 days of appointment, if applicable.
keywords: coordinate with other U.S. agencies and international organizations
strategy: Skip this one: it requires a year at GS-14 level in direct supervision, international technical assistance and public financial management, and his work has been domestic emergency management and public health.

watch_outs: The required international PFM technical assistance experience does not appear in Daniel's known background, so a 'not qualified' rating is likely.

The Secret clearance and financial disclosure add time to hiring, and the role requires some travel plus a commute from Manassas to DC despite telework eligibility.
